about: The closed list of failure ids fgos-config produces. YAML Document refusals pass through with their own rule id and are listed in packages/yaml-doc/contracts/refusal-rules.v1.json, never copied here.

codes.meaning: config.yaml and config.json both exist in one scope.
The file revision changed between read and write, or the write lock stayed held.
A change that differs from the standard carries no usable reason.
A confined session called a write door.
A config file or .fgos directory is a symlink or resolves outside its root.
An account pool or the gateway token sits in a config file.
A confined worker called a verb that needs the account pool.
A config file does not parse or breaks strict-config.
The effective value fails a section schema; names the schema path and keyword, never the value.
A key sits in a file its scope does not allow, or on or above a global-only path.
A write was aimed at a legacy config.json.
The platform has no no-follow open, so a file rule cannot be enforced.
The gateway token file is a symlink or not regular, wider than 0600, or not exactly one line of printable ASCII; the reason keyword (symlink, mode, shape) says which, never the value.
The removal stage of a key move was called without the machine check: it needs the owner's statement that no release on this machine reads the keys from the global file.
The accounts file or the token file already holds different data than the global file's key (or, for the removal stage, none); names the file and the key path, never a value.

reserved-prefixes.meaning: Rule ids: each is a $defs entry of config-schema.meta.v1.json (up to the first dot) or a rule in src/lint.rs.
Rule ids of src/lint.rs: standard-orphan, standard-forbidden-key, standard-invalid.

not-produced-here.meaning: The native addon is missing on the channel; the door names it, this crate never sees it.
